title: Whistleblowing reports to the SRA protected under PIDA
summary: The SRA is a prescribed person under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998. This means people who work for or with SRA-regulated firms are legally protected when they report wrongdoing to the SRA.
what_changes: The SRA has been designated as a prescribed person under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998.
Protection covers anyone working for or with an SRA-regulated firm or individual, including paralegals, clerks, trainees and agency workers.
The person making the report must reasonably believe they are acting in the public interest.
Protected disclosures must relate to wrongdoing by people or firms the SRA regulates, whether past, current or likely in future.
who_it_applies_to: All SRA-regulated firms and individuals, and the employees and agency workers who work for or with them.

history.event: SRA designated as a prescribed person under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998.
